biography.plain_text: Alexander Gennadyevich Khloponin is a Russian businessman and former senior politician. He led Norilsk Nickel from 1996 to 2001, served as governor of Taimyr and Krasnoyarsk, and was Russia's deputy prime minister from 2010 to 2018. His business wealth came from a stake in Norilsk Nickel, sold before his move into politics.

long_biography.plain_text:
At 31, Alexander Khloponin took charge of Norilsk Nickel when low metal prices and Soviet-era management practices had left the producer in crisis. He introduced market disciplines, oversaw restructuring and helped restore the company to international competitiveness. The role also made him wealthy: before leaving business, he sold a personal holding in the miner.

Khloponin had trained in international economics and worked at Vnesheconombank before joining the International Finance Company, where he rose to president. He then chose public office, winning governorships in Taimyr and Krasnoyarsk. In 2010 he became both deputy prime minister and presidential envoy to the North Caucasus; he remained deputy prime minister until 2018. His career therefore joined operating experience in metals and banking with unusually long service in regional and federal government.
